Recompute a manifest's recorded statistics against the data

Source: R/repro.R
mnfrcmp.Rd

Re-evaluates named statistics against data and compares each to what the manifest recorded. This is the check vrfcps() cannot make: that one confirms the record is internally consistent, which an edited-at-the-time manifest also is. Use it when receiving a capsule, or after a data refresh, to confirm that the numbers in the record still come out of the data.

Usage

mnfrcmp(man, data, stats, tol = NULL)

Arguments

man

A manifest, as from mkmnf() and recrd().

data

The data the statistics are computed from (usually a data frame); passed unchanged to each function.

stats

Named list of functions of data, each returning one value. Names must match the recorded result names.

tol

Optional numeric tolerance (absolute) overriding each result's own recorded tol. Supply it to check more strictly than the original run did. NULL (the default) uses the recorded one.

Value

A list of class c("bricklayer_recompute", "list"):

ok

logical, every statistic matched and none was left unchecked.

results

data frame, one row per recomputed statistic, with the columns name (character), recorded and recomputed (numeric, NA for non-numeric values), delta (numeric absolute difference), tol (numeric), status ("MATCH", "DIFFER", "NOT_RECORDED" or "ERROR") and detail (character explanation).

unchecked

character, the names recorded but not recomputed.

Details

Every recorded result that was NOT recomputed is reported too, as unchecked. An analysis that recorded twenty statistics and re-derives three has seventeen it has not re-derived, and a report that quietly omitted them would read as a clean bill of health.

For each function in stats, its value on data is compared with the observed value recorded under the same name. Numeric results match when they are identical (so the same NA, NaN or infinite value on both sides matches) or when \(|recorded - recomputed| \le tol\), with tol the argument if given, else the result's recorded tol, else 0 (exact); any other pair with a missing or non-finite value is "DIFFER". A non-numeric result (a label, a verdict) is compared as text and must be identical. A function that errors gives the status "ERROR" with the message; a name the manifest does not have gives "NOT_RECORDED". ok is TRUE only when every row is "MATCH" and nothing recorded was left unchecked. The functions are run as given, so they can read files or draw random numbers; nothing else is changed.

Errors: man not a list with results; stats not a non-empty fully named list, or with an element that is not a function.

See also

vrfcps(), cpsfals(), recrd().

Examples

d <- data.frame(x = 1:10)
m <- mkmnf(list(dataset = "demo"), env = FALSE)
m <- recrd(m, "mean_x", obs = mean(d$x), expd = 5.5)
#>   mean_x                                       observed = 5.5000       expected = 5.5000       [INFO]
m <- recrd(m, "n", obs = nrow(d), expd = 10)
#>   n                                            observed = 10.0000      expected = 10.0000      [INFO]

# recomputing both reproduces them
res <- mnfrcmp(m, d, list(mean_x = function(z) mean(z$x),
                                     n = function(z) nrow(z)))
res$ok
#> [1] TRUE
res$results[, c("name", "recorded", "recomputed", "status")]
#>     name recorded recomputed status
#> 1 mean_x      5.5        5.5  MATCH
#> 2      n     10.0       10.0  MATCH

# recomputing one leaves the other reported as unchecked
mnfrcmp(m, d, list(n = function(z) nrow(z)))$unchecked
#> [1] "mean_x"

# and data that no longer matches the record is caught
mnfrcmp(m, data.frame(x = 1:11),
                   list(n = function(z) nrow(z)))$ok
#> [1] FALSE

# a stricter tolerance than the recorded one
mnfrcmp(m, d, list(mean_x = function(z) mean(z$x) + 1e-9,
                              n = nrow), tol = 0)$results$status
#> [1] "DIFFER" "MATCH" 

# a function that fails is reported, not thrown
mnfrcmp(m, d, list(mean_x = function(z) stop("column y is gone"),
                              n = nrow))$results[, c("name", "status")]
#>     name status
#> 1 mean_x  ERROR
#> 2      n  MATCH

# statistics must be named
try(mnfrcmp(m, d, list(function(z) nrow(z))))
#> Error : `stats` must be a non-empty named list of functions
